notes.title: Patch #22: Just One More Patch – (Spoiler: It’s Never Just One)
notes.notes:
Hello hello, we've got some fixes and qol changes here from a game that isn't taking legal action against anyone!

Bug Fixes:
[list]
[*] Delivery vehicles sometimes driving past an open parking bay and instead circling the block.
[*] The Garage UI not updating properly after changes are made to the products delivered by that garage / vehicle.
[*] Products stuck on the ground will be despawned after 5 minutes.
[*] The time speed was not being taken into account during cleaning tasks, meaning cleaning up a product at x3 speed took the same amount of time as cleaning up a product at x1 speed.
[*] If a garage was deleted, the next garage would inherit the previously deleted garage’s sorting color and some other additional settings.
[*] Garages’ order (within the garage’s list to the left of the dispatch map) could change after saving and reloading the game. They are now ordered consistently.
[*] Removed a parking spot from Seal Avenue which workers were unable to collect products from.
[*] Pressing esc during room construction / deletion would cause the build cost / space indicators to be stuck on screen.
[/list]

QOL:
[list]
[*] Garages are now sorted by oldest to newest. If the sorting color of a garage is changed it will go to the bottom of the list for its new sorting color.
[*] If a delivery destination is removed from a vehicle whilst it is parked there, it will leave to go to the next destination.
[*] Play an animation on a newly hired employee within the list & also when an employee’s sorting color is changed to highlight the new / modified employee.
[/list]

Tutorial Bug Fixes:
[list]
[*] Tutorial landscaping objects were not spawning when starting a new game.
[*] Tutorial door placement indicators remaining in place even after placing a door in the correct position.
[*] Saving and reloading the game multiple times during the tutorial would cause the in-world tutorial indicators (e.g. the arrows above employees) to either not display or be positioned incorrectly.
[*] During the tutorial, players would be able to place the staff room door leading into the WC instead of the intended position leading into the kitchen.
[*] In-world green tutorial indicators would remain in place even if the applicable object’s placement was cancelled.
[*] When cancelling the placement of a tutorial object, the button indicating that the object needed to be placed would stop animating unless the menu was closed and reopened.
[*] The optional tutorial panel was closed if it was open when the player completed the optional tutorial segment.
[/list]

Tutorial Polish:
[list]
[*] During the tutorial, snap objects into place if they are moved into the correct position and rotation.
[*] Remove the green tutorial placement indicators if an object is moved into the correct position and rotation.
[*] Removed objects’ grid occupations indicator for tutorial objects, it’s cleaner just to have the green indicator showing the outline of the object.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch #21: Keeping you coming back for more
notes.notes:
Greetings Kingpins!

We've been in the lab and here's an assortment of user interface changes and bug fixes!

[h3]New Employee Management setting[/h3]
[list]
[*] A button to re-hire dead employee's has been added. When your employees die, a button will be appear in their place, allowing you to replace their feeble entity with a new employee with the same equipment, room group, schedule and task settings. If you do not want to re-hire them, you can dismiss them.
[*] A button to duplicate employee settings. Once you've hired an employee with their tasks, equipment and room, there is now a button to duplicate them with all of their settings!
[/list]

[h3]Save Backup system[/h3]
[list]
[*] Your ten most recent saves for a game will now be retained.
[*] The load menu will show the most recent save by default
[*] When deleting saves, you can choose to delete an individual save, or all instances of a world and game.
[/list]

[h3]Qol Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Area of Effect emitters  such as heaters will now be removed if a new room group is painted over them, previously only objects that belonged in the room would be removed. 
[*] A tooltip appears when hovering over product logos on the dispatch map. 
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Employees' positions within the employee list are now consistent. Newly hired employees will go to the bottom of the list. When an employee’s sorting colour is changed, they will go to the bottom of that sorting colour's list.
[*] Employees were sometimes not properly appearing within the list if they were at the top or bottom of the viewable area of the list.
[*] If a plot business types was changed, the finance panel would only display the new plot type's finance even when viewing previous days' income which would result in a mismatch.
[*] Time speed was not affecting characters' needs depletion, now when playing at the respective speeds, the needs will deplete correctly.
[*] Made load game UI larger to accommodate for certain localisations that were previously cut off.
[/list]

Hello Kingpins, to keep you all in the dope loop here's a  list of what we're cooking for you in the latest batch of fixes, with a smidge of chilli pepper for that extra kick.

[u][b]Bug Fixes:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*]Fix to products sometimes being invisible.
[*]Fix to vehicles sometimes taking very long detours when ‘circling the block’ if there was no parking available when they reached their delivery destination.
[*]Fix to delivery destinations (cash and special clients) being assigned to vehicles that are sometimes not being saved so the destinations would need to be reassigned after reloading the game.
[*] Fix to various issues when waiters were interacting with customers at the Lobster Restaurant tables.
[*] Fix to products clipping through the shelves within the trucks.
[*] Fix to ‘Expand character configuration panel’ tutorial indicator sometimes being displayed at the incorrect time.

[u][b]QOL:[/b][/u]

[*] Drop down selectors have been implemented for assigning Schedules and Room Groups to characters, which should be a big QoL improvement when many schedules and room groups have been created.

notes.title: Starting your business on a high!
notes.notes:
[h1]Five top tips to start your business on a high[/h1]

Definitely Not Fried Chicken is a deceptively deep simulation. From NPCs with complex needs to an intricate interlocking economy, there’s a lot to explore and experiment with. In order to do that you’ll need to quickly build a successful foundation for your narcotic empire, so here are five essential tips that will help you go from conquering the tutorial to being king of the city as efficiently as possible.

[h2]Look after your workers[/h2]

This sounds obvious but is easy to overlook in the scramble to start pumping weed onto the streets. The tutorial shows you how to build a bathroom and break room for chicken shop employees, but don’t forget the same applies to ALL your workers. Yes, even the ones slaving away in your weed factories.And one of the biggest early game hurdles is ensuring you don’t keep losing staff. Here’s an easy way to help stop that happening.

Get in the habit of adding toilets, breakrooms, kitchens and bedrooms to everything you build. These don’t need to be fancy in terms of amenities- just the basics will do to start with - but having them on-site for every location you control will mean your workers are able to keep themselves fed and rested. And this means they’ll stick around, and you’ll have uninterrupted production.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/ea2b2f4da931c143d241ac5a349e7d6826614123.png[/img]

[h2]Don’t fear the schedules[/h2]

Look, we get it. Nobody gets into the drug trade because they love scheduling but - trust us - it’s the secret to a sustainable business, so don’t overlook this incredible tool. You see, the workers in the game are actually super dedicated. Psychotically so, in fact. Unless you tell them otherwise, they’ll keep on trying to do whatever they’ve been assigned until they’re literally ravenous with hunger or delirious from exhaustion. That’s when they get angry and quit, or - worst case scenario - they just drop dead on the floor.

Setting a schedule for each worker as soon as you hire them means you can not only stop that happening, but also gives you greater control over your business. It doesn’t take long to do - just tick or untick the box for each hour of the day. Giving them regular breaks every four hours or so means they can take advantage of the food and recreation spaces you’ve built. Setting up overlapping shifts for multiple workers means you’re always open 24-7, even while your day staff take a well-earned sleep.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/a48aa7591aa0559eb7dea5922c6acce44e603561.png[/img]

[h2]Tackle one delivery at a time[/h2]

So you’ve got your first little weed factory up and running, and boxes of pungent green are filling up your storeroom. Then the calls start coming in. Customers! Fantastic - time to start making that fortune! Tag them all on the map and let your delivery rider get to work! Right?

Wrong. You need to prioritize your deliveries. Some customers only want two boxes. Some want eight, or even more. You won’t get paid until you’ve delivered everything they asked for, and if your driver is having to split their attention between multiple active customers, that just means it’ll be even longer until any of them hand over the cheddar. 

So, at the start of your career, accept each order - they won’t have time limits to begin with, and will happily wait - but then only keep one active at a time on the map. Click on your garage on the map, then on the customer. This will ensure that the driver only delivers to that customer until they pay out. As you add more drivers, use this feature to make sure each one is servicing the most cost efficient orders.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/2a05ddc979cdbdac26033ed43f09291017969140.png[/img]

Tackle the lower numbers first, the customers who’ll only need a couple of trips before they pay out. Then work through the higher orders (no pun intended). A little planning and patience at this stage will mean you gradually build up your bank balance rather than watching it diminish every day.

[h2]Expand your empire the smart way[/h2]

Once you’ve got a nice tight little routine going on, with happy efficient workers piling up stock and methodical deliveries bringing in a steady flow of cash, it’s time to start expanding your horizons. There are two key ways of doing this.

First, buy the cheapest plots to build more drug factories. Be smart though - you don’t need to start building on that land right away. Each new chunk of land owned lets you hire two more workers for the shady side of your business, regardless of whether you build more factory buildings. Use that to your advantage and supercharge the business you’ve already got, hiring new workers and delivering to more existing customers faster. This will accelerate your financial growth, until you’re in a position to undertake the second stage of smart expansion.

Buying vacant commercial land, meanwhile, enables you to set up your first “front” business. To start with this will be a laundromat, so follow the tips above to create a location where workers will be fed, rested and happy. Make sure you add a stockroom, and start using your delivery drivers to move product through there as well as direct to your existing clients. Soon enough, these front businesses will be producing an even steadier cashflow, setting you up to really start growing your empire with new drug factories and more ambitious fronts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/a21923bfe7675319be422a8e84efa7322a1d331c.png[/img]

[h2]Expand and acquire to accelerate progress[/h2]

You’re not limited to just dealing to phone customers and selling through your fronts. You can also select fixed locations such as the university, gun shop and scrapyard as delivery spots and regularly shift product through those. Doing this will unlock new abilities and technology, as well as better weapons to keep your guards competitive as you attract more heat.

The Monuments tab at the top of the screen is worth investigating as well, once your cash reserves are healthy. As well as the Order Hotline you use to attract phone customers, there are lots of other perks you can invest in around the city. Buying the gym will toughen up your guards, while the construction site will lower the cost of any new building work - very useful as you construct more elaborate drug factories and large front businesses. You can even buy billboards to drive more customers through your legitimate businesses, which in turn means more drugs sold through them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/4c04c662c6bda9fe06340097ef991eeed0e0fa4b.png[/img]

[h2]Experiment and have fun![/h2]

By this point you should be well established as both a purveyor of narcotics and an entrepreneur in the laundry and fast food industries. So now’s the time to take off those training wheels and see what you can really do. Try developing higher quality merchandise in your factories, make your chicken and lobster restaurants the talk of the town, or just keep growing your client base, accruing more and more of the ol’ folding green stuff. The world is yours!

notes.title: Hotfix 006
notes.notes:
Good morning Corporate Chemists,

[b]AI Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Workers not serving customers at the cash register properly.
[*] If a customer's preferred drug is out of stock, workers will no longer offer another drug which is also out of stock.
[*] Products not made in equal numbers (e.g. not making all kinds of donuts despite having the equipment and workers to do so).
[*] Characters getting stuck on their way to and from business plots.
[*] Characters getting stuck in the same place in an idle loop, even with work to do.
[*] Characters getting stuck when moving from the head of the queue to start using an appliance.
[*] Various additional fail safes for general AI issues.
[*] Vehicles not being able to navigate to the Robot Factory to deliver to the workers there.
[*] Cleaners will now clean up soda / drink / laundry detergent products that have been dropped by workers.
[*] Guns would not fire after re-loading the game.
[*] Character death animation would re-play upon re-loading the game (now dead characters will not appear at all upon re-loading).
[*] Under certain circumstances clients would not pick up delivered boxes from vehicles and aimlessly walk around instead.
[/list]

[b]Gameplay Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Not being able to see how many of each drug type has been delivered to an order (you can now select each drug to see how many have been delivered directly on the map).
[*] Drug delivery numbers disappearing when a delivery was made to a separate client.
[*] Players not being able to purchase additional sub-plots, despite having the money to do so.
[*] Character names now do not change upon re-loading the game.
[*] Characters cannot be fired during an attack to stop the attack prematurely.
[*] Attacks would be skipped if other dialogue was loaded (e.g. tutorial dialogue).
[*] Hotline orders disappearing from the scroll area (to the right of the map) after re-loading a save.
[*] Hitting the spacebar would re-press the most recent button / toggle pressed.
[*] No task description would be shown for cleaners and engineers within the employee rows UI.
[*] Removed some 'Translation Key Not Found' error messages.
[/list]

[b]New Features[/b]
[list]
[*] Floors now get dirty as they are walked over, eventually the cleaner will clean them if they get too dirty. Dirty floors lower hygiene level of workers who work around them.
[*] Additional cosmetic doors, including double doors to make businesses look nicer.
[/list]

[b]Balance[/b]
[list]
[*] Now only Cannabis will be served at the Laundromat and Donut Shop. Meth will be served at the Chicken Shop and Lobster Restaurant (coming during early access). Cocaine will be served at the Nightclub and Casino (both coming during early access).
[*] If a customer's preferred drug is out of stock, workers will upsell to the highest value drug (of the same type) which is currently in stock.
[*] Tweaked a few values to lower business running costs.
[/list]

[b]Other[/b]
[list]
[*] More detailed work descriptions for cleaners.
[*] Allowed the sink to be placed in business staff breakout rooms so cups and plates can be washed up rather than always dropped on the floor.
[*] Hotline customer name displayed instead of 'An NPC' when a new hotline order comes in + changed the character icon to be a phone.
[/list]

- Nick.

notes.title: Character AI Expanded
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Last time we had a look at the character AI beind the scenes of DNFC. We'll expand on that a little further today and talk about behaviour trees. We use modified trees for different character types, namely employees, customers and attackers. Some are shared by all like death sequences, and some are unique like shift patterns for employees. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/XCFMXyy.gif[/img]

Certain behaviours, such as “needs” are removed entirely for attackers; we didn’t want them to start dying of hunger or wetting themselves mid attack, as funny as this is, surely they would have sorted themselves out before arriving guns blazing.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/UhWQ8HO.gif[/img]

You will notice lots of characters walking the streets, some are customers using the complex behaviour trees and some are very simple pedestrians with no behaviour tree - simply walking between two buildings to help fill out the streets. This allows us to reduce the number of complex characters in the world, yet make the world feel just as lived in. 

When the player creates a business, complex customers for that specific business are spawned in nearby buildings and walk directly to that business. This allows us to easily control customer numbers based on the business’ rating. As the player builds more businesses more complex customers are spawned; we start to reduce the number of simple pedestrians in the world so the total number of characters in the world stays roughly the same. 

This decision is made when a simple pedestrian arrives at their destination, despawning them if the current total has exceeded a threshold. If however they are not despawned, they are instead teleported to a random building in the map and given a new destination to walk to. This is another little performance saver as we don’t even have to remove the character from the scene only to make a new one on the very same frame.

We hope you enjoyed that insight into the inner working of our many pedestrians!

notes.title: Character AI
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Time for another dev diary post and we're diving into what makes the characters tick!

When the world of Definitely Not Fried Chicken is in full motion, the map will be filled with hundreds of complex characters navigating and participating in the world; from visiting player businesses to walking the streets. 

Characters must react to their “needs”, respond to alerts such as fires or attacks and keep tabs on what work is available if they’re an employee. In order to do this we’ve utilised behaviour trees to give structure to the priority in which tasks are executed. 

For example, if an employee is desperately hungry they will prioritise making a sandwich over doing work. If an attacker were to burst through the door at this very same moment however, the employee would forget about the sandwich and run away from the attacker. While running away, if the employee’s bladder stat reaches zero, they would then pause to wet themselves before continuing to run away. The poor guy just wanted a sandwich...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/7d98345154bc2690d721a71f44441e59d56c60e7.png[/img]

Behaviour trees allow us to more easily create these complicated behaviours, although it certainly isn’t trivial given the range of possibilities; resulting in large trees with many branches. 

In terms of performance we couldn’t run such complicated behaviours for every character every frame. So we spread the computation over a number of seconds resulting in a few trees being updated every frame. 

This works well as we don’t mind if there’s a slight delay in the character's realising they need the toilet for example. Other scenarios might demand more instant reactions such as gun battles, in which case we update a character’s behaviour immediately after they’ve been killed so we get their death animation to play without a delay.

Thanks for reading and we'll see you next time!

Everything you need to protect your premises. The secured doors you put down won’t last forever but at least they’ll delay any old nobody from waltzing on into your undercover drug den.

It would be wise to keep in mind that intruders aren’t going to go completely out of their way to break through that one door on the other side of the facility. If they can’t easily access a door and have the right equipment, they might just blow a hole in the wall instead.

notes.title: Vehicles

Continuing the theme of looking at the technical bits and pieces that make up the world of Definitely Not Fried Chicken, today we're looking at vehicles!

Vehicles will be an important element of the world map since they will populate a large portion of the world, moving and interacting with one another. It was really important to gather plenty of references in order to have enough variation in the designs. 
The first step of making every vehicle was establishing how much room characters would need to sit within them. By creating the seating and dashboard first it allowed us to figure out roughly how big a car would be, and eventually became the starting point of most vehicles.

notes.title: Building the world of Fried Chicken
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

The world of Fried Chicken is full of wacky characters, but they all need a place to live and work! Our artist Filip is on the job, crafting only the most suspicious of shop fronts, and stunning beach front flats around the city. 

The first step for creating any asset is figuring out the dimensions and unit sizes with both help to inform appropriate references. Since the game is based on Miami a lot of references came from the city itself; it’s full of colour and we wanted to get the across the vibrancy. After getting an idea of the asset direction each building can be broken down into modular pieces and assembled in MagicaVoxel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/798f23a18163ef339a2942572cdf074e1ae392f0.png[/img]

Examples of the kind of references gathered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/d3831377a86d99820b1090202e55829e5eaacbff.png[/img]

All buildings are built with a modular approach, such that many separate 3D pieces that can be easily put together in multiple ways to create an assortment of complete buildings. This was the best approach in order to get lots of variation and make production efficient. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/b809cf1e083110368f19092c2435876740c49824.png[/img]

Asset packs are made up of walls, doors and rooftops along with other special assets like ladders, ventilation, electrical utilities etc. which help really bring the buildings to life and set them in the world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/2bcda46c5207e83effd8c43730ed6c06a1e2e941.png[/img]

Each building falls into a different category, these being residential, commercial or industrial. These each have slightly different visual rules in order to make sure they can be easily identified by the player.

notes.title: The World Map
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

We're going to zoom out a bit today and have a look at the world map for DNFC, there's a whole world outside the walls of your business. and they want what you're selling!

Early designs of the game considered having a huge map with hundreds of plots and a vast number of businesses that could be duplicated all around. This size was however at odds with the smaller scale viewing and management of your simulated people, their “needs” and their reactions; all of which would be missed by players when witnessing the world from far away over a huge landscape. 

There was plenty to gain from reducing down such as an in depth product quality system, employee management controls, and tower defense design to name but a few. On top of this, the world itself could become more intricate and hand crafted. 

The final map has different areas to the city; suburbs and farms in the west, industry and ports to the south, high rise downtown and beachfront bars to the East. There are many places players can choose to set up their businesses, with each new plot offering different business types to develop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/6a764ed49d2833d6c8db386c475ea6dd93b97d4b.png[/img]

The first map prototype had a small central compound with 2 business plots available to purchase. At this stage we knew we wanted to have a beach out to the East, shown in beige and industry and Port areas down South shown in brown.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/18fa898de8854a80302e5aeb3c200375346e21f8.png[/img]

Further on in development we made substantial progress to achieving the beachfront and industry areas we desired. We had also made good progress creating suburban and commercial districts too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/8cc627ef973ca46329837a7cb44b34ea72cdd893.png[/img]

Here is a more recent shot of the map with more areas filled in and the port area complete. We still need to do more work to make the player plots (in brown) look more interesting than an empty patch of dirt. You can see the large central compound in the centre. This is actually split into subplots allowing the player to expand their central drug facility over time as their business empire grows.

notes.title: Fire and Explosions
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Great tasting chicken and moreish drugs are of course vital to success, but all is for nothing if you don't maintain your equipment!

Under maintained appliances and explosive weaponry can lead to fires breaking out. For anyone standing nearby this leads to utter chaos as workers run around wildly and engineers scramble to put out the flames. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Q6f5Jfy.gif[/img]

Anyone standing too close for too long will become ignited and face imminent death as they run around on fire. More advanced machinery can become unstable if left in unsuitable environmental conditions for too long, for example the automatic meth distiller requires cold surroundings else it‘ll overheat and explode causing a significant fire to erupt. 

If multiple unstable machines are placed in a row and one blows, this can lead to a chain reaction of devastation unravelling through the facility. It is vital to keep an engineer or two nearby to ensure good maintenance levels, unstable appliances have satisfactory environmental conditions and ensure appropriate spacing to reduce the chance of chain reactions. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/943c5b4cdf1a8dfcbb6ae553d0f09750af0ae9f8.gif[/img]

Finally, barring such appliances behind secure doors might be a good idea; you can be sure that any would-be attacker’s first target to cause maximum disruption will be the more volatile equipment...

So when you get to creating your own business empire in Definitely Not Fried Chicken, make sure to keep a close eye on your equipment - a huge fire can really throw a spanner in the works!

notes.title: Clients and the DAE
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

There's two elements out there in Definitely Not Fried Chicken that can have a serious impact on your drugs business; your clients and the DAE (Drugs Abduction Establishment). This leads us to the combat mechanic in-game.

Initial ideas around combat involved having overly complicated systems around suspicion and police inspections. notes.title: From Dope Loop to Definitely Not Fried Chicken!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

We've had some eally good insights into DNFC's staff on the last few dev diaries so we're changing pace a bit and taking you through the process of coming up with the logo and name for the game!

The logo and name went through countless iterations. The original name for the game in the initial pitch was Dopeloop, and still remains on the name of builds and project files. It was short and simple, but for new players it didn’t communicate the business cover up operation theme the game was going for. 

People would often ask us to repeat the name, with the words “Dope” and “Loop” becoming misheard when said together quickly, and as such the meaning of the game being lost. The quest for a new name had begun; over the next months numerous names came and went, but we would always circle back round to Dopeloop despite its drawbacks, even going so far as to make a number of different logos.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/81d424bbf629e22999eeb7c1df164e731bccdd81.png[/img]

We began to iterate on logo designs, despite the name difficulties. One idea involved a badge or name tag to represent those worn by workers in the game’s businesses: The Chicken Shop, and hence the chicken head on the badge. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/3a0de04bbd0e4c5bdc7dfda23ba7c9f64496d935.png[/img]

The Chicken Shop was always top of the list when it came to businesses we wanted to include in the game as it seemed to perfectly fit the theme of cover up drug businesses; some definite Breaking Bad influences there. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/5eac58baea90ae2cef3200b43a4287b3db2f0c64.gif[/img]

From the badge came the idea of a factory style sign. This was around the same time we were considering just focussing the game solely on one plot that would be your drug factory, with no city or surrounding businesses. Ultimately the factory ended up becoming the central compound where the drug production takes place, and the sign concept formed the basis of the final logo once we settled on the new name.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/2bf5fced553b9b236830e784059794dd3beb7636.jpg[/img]

The driving force behind the new name was to get across the idea that everything is not as it seems, giving rise to the “Definitely Not” part of the name. Sticking with the Chicken Shop idea from previous concepts it was only logical to directly reference that part too, and as such “Definitely Not Fried Chicken” came to be. 

Further touches to really strengthen the theme included using spray paint for the “Definitely Not” text, as if someone wanted to expose the Fried Chicken factory. Silhouette icons below hinted to businesses in the game such as donut and ice cream shops as well as the weapons needed to defend your compound. Finally the abbreviation “Inc.” was added as a hint to players that this was a simulation game with production style gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/d326134abc0b3ba79ddfb5584522c74ee6605448.png[/img]

We hope you enjoyed that journey through the various iterations of names and logos we went through!

notes.title: Sickness
notes.notes:
Good hygiene is more important than ever right now, and it's no different in Definitely Not Fried Chicken. You'll need to ensure your staff are able to maintain good hygiene to keep your business running and your customers happy (and safe!).

When a character’s hygiene becomes low, they will start to emit stink lines and flies will begin to circle them. If their hygiene reaches zero they will become sick and turn green. At this point they will then start to throw up onto the floor, with each successive vomiting increasing the chance of death. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/7A5iR7V.gif[/img]

When sick characters pick up products, the product will become contaminated, reducing it’s value, or in the case of food businesses cause the customer to become sick when they eat it, potentially leading to some quite messy results. To help mitigate against this, characters can be equipped with latex gloves to stop them contaminating products.

Today we want to tell you about some of the environmental effects that will come into play in the game, and how they might impact your day to day operations.

Using heatmaps the player will be able to view a series of different effects that spread within each facility due to placed equipment or environmental controllers. These include temperature, lighting, humidity, air pressure and toxic gases.

notes.title: Definitely NOT Employee of the Month
notes.notes:
Hey Chicken Champions! It's time for another dev diary :-)

Last time we learned about balancing the needs of our staff, this week we're going to look a little deeper in who our staff are.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/d2c4c6b9f4d35ce7d9bef6311868c481c3e5cbce.gif[/img]

The game has four distinct employee types; Worker, Engineer, Cleaner and Guard. Workers craft products and serve customers, Engineers maintain appliances, reset traps and put out fires, Cleaners keep floors clean reducing contamination, and Guards protect facilities from attackers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/4c326a6fb1c9dd5b53d408667c2225b83c572260.gif[/img]

Early on in the design process we considered having just a single hirable employee type, who could be assigned any number of roles such as fixing equipment or protecting the facility. It was decided however that splitting the employees into distinct roles more clearly highlighted the four different gameplay aspects within facility design and operation. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/f1794cd3a33b72018df86db95b74458e355361d8.gif[/img]

Additionally, this opened up opportunities to include commands specific to an employee type, such as assigning individual product lines for Workers, and patrol routes for Guards. Having this clear distinction also improved the game’s UI, with each employee types’ actions being appropriately represented in the side panel.

notes.title: The human element
notes.notes:
Definitely Not Fried Chicken tasks you with growing your drugs empire by succesfully managing a legitimate business - the iconic fried chicken joint. Today we want to introduce you to a key element of that unique business plan, your loyal staff. 

A core part of the game we wanted to include from the beginning was sims like character “needs”. Without satisfying each of the 5 “needs”: hunger, bladder, hygiene, fun, and energy employees will become less productive and eventually die in different ways. 

Some scenarios are more simple, providing no food sources will cause employees to go hungry and die from starvation. Others can lead to more complicated behaviours, no toilets and employees soil themselves, bottoming out their hygiene. With nowhere to wash, employees may become sick and if left untreated for too long death will be just around the corner. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/8459044ea952d8861a0d2ba31269c90c580884f7.gif[/img]

All employees need some fun every once in a while, without it they might start to go a bit crazy… screaming, crying, rocking in a corner; it may all get a bit too much with some deciding to end it all. Finally, with reduced energy comes slower movement and production speeds, everyone likes a refreshing coffee break to perk them up again. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39744790/89a9deb680bee79e1803617018c49bb2e7d70030.gif[/img]

Too many coffees however and you will witness the mad toilet dash, so best to make sure a bathroom is always in reach. With no beds or coffees employees will be too tired to safely operate dangerous machinery, which may lead to their demise.

Make employee care one of your secret herbs and spices!

notes.title: Definitely Not Fried Chicken is definitely not about selling hard drugs
notes.notes:
Let's say, hypothetically, that you had decided to open up a front business in order to hide an illegal drug manufacturing and distribution operation. How about a fried chicken restaurant? You'd have to serve great chicken, of course - but you'd also need to keep a close eye on the back of the house, so to speak. That's the idea behind Definitely Not Fried Chicken, a whimsical and brightly coloured game about selling hard drugs.

If the premise seems familiar, that's probably because it's more or less the same deal that Gustavo Fring had going in the AMC television series Breaking Bad. In Definitely Not Fried Chicken, the tone is much more tongue-in-cheek - the bright, blocky art style gives everything a very cheerful mood, even when you're arming employees to the teeth in order to protect your business assets from pesky cops, or building new cannabis growing facilities.

Developer Dope Games says Definitely Not Fried Chicken is "the ultimate in drug empire strategy and simulation", but it's also quick to point out that it doesn't take itself too seriously. And when you have people in chicken mascot costumes helping with your meth production, it's hard not to laugh, right?
